title: Pull Cord Lamp
summary: Dragging the bead stretches a rubber-banded cord past a latch point that toggles a soft conical beam, then the cord rings back to rest on an underdamped spring.
choreography: 0-170ms: the bead is pulled 38 units down with an ease-out cubic (or follows the pointer with exponential resistance, max 60); the shade dips 8% of the pull.
At 26 units the latch fires once: beam and halo fade in over 320ms (out over 160ms), the shade takes a velocity kick, and the latch only re-arms below 11 units.
On release the cord rings back at ~2Hz with about 40% overshoot above rest, bowing sideways while slack; the pull settles in ~1s and the slower 1Hz sway fades over ~2s.
agentPrompt:
Model the cord end as a 2D point with displacement from rest; while dragging map pointer delta through a rubber band (y: 60 * (1 - exp(-dy/60)), x: 34 * tanh(dx/70)) and on release integrate two springs per frame with 4ms substeps: pull axis k=170 c=7.5, sway axis k=38 c=3.
Toggle the lamp once when the pull exceeds 26 units and re-arm only after it drops below 11 (hysteresis), so one pull is one click; a tap or keypress plays a 170ms ease-out pull to 38 units and then hands off to the same spring.
Draw the cord as an SVG quadratic whose control point lags by velocity (clamp(vx * 0.04, +-14)) and bows by 0.55x the slack when the bead bounces above rest; rotate the bead to the curve's end tangent.
Light is opacity only: a blurred trapezoid with a vertical warm-white gradient plus a radial halo, 320ms in and 160ms out; run a gentle auto-pull every 4.5s until the first user input and stop the rAF loop when the energy reaches zero.

<!-- Pull Cord Lamp: elastic drag + damped spring snap-back + threshold latch -->
<svg id="lamp" viewBox="0 0 360 260" style="background:#111113;touch-action:none">
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="beam" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
      <stop offset="0" stop-color="#fff4dc" stop-opacity=".7"/>
      <stop offset="1" stop-color="#fff4dc" stop-opacity="0"/>
    </linearGradient>
    <filter id="soft"><feGaussianBlur stdDeviation="7"/></filter>
  </defs>
  <polygon class="light" points="142,88 218,88 286,226 74,226" fill="url(#beam)" filter="url(#soft)"/>
  <path class="dome" d="M136 90Q130 90 130 83C130 52 152 36 180 36C208 36 230 52 230 83Q230 90 224 90Z"/>
  <circle class="bulb" cx="180" cy="95" r="14"/>
  <path class="cord" fill="none" stroke="#86868c" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round"/>
  <rect class="bead" x="-6.5" y="-1" width="13" height="22" rx="6.5" fill="#96969c"/>
</svg>

<style>
  #lamp .light { opacity: 0; transition: opacity .3s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1); }
  #lamp .dome  { fill: #5c5c61; transition: fill .2s; }
  #lamp .bulb  { fill: #38383c; transition: fill .12s; }
  #lamp.on .light { opacity: 1; }
  #lamp.on .dome  { fill: #a9a9ae; }
  #lamp.on .bulb  { fill: #fff; }
  #lamp .bead { cursor: grab; }
</style>

<script>
  const svg = document.getElementById('lamp');
  const cord = svg.querySelector('.cord'), bead = svg.querySelector('.bead');
  const AX = 211, AY = 64, LEN = 100;   // anchor + rest length
  const MAX = 60, CLICK = 26;           // max stretch, switch threshold
  let bx = 0, by = 0, vx = 0, vy = 0, latch = false, drag = null, last = performance.now();

  function frame(now) {
    const dt = Math.min(0.034, (now - last) / 1000); last = now;
    for (let n = 8, h = dt / 8; n--;) {
      if (!drag) {
        vy += (-170 * by - 7.5 * vy) * h; by += vy * h;   // pull axis: zeta ~0.29, rings ~1s
        vx += (-38 * bx - 3 * vx) * h;    bx += vx * h;   // sway axis: slow pendulum
      }
      // Latch with hysteresis: one toggle per pull, re-arms below 42% of the threshold.
      if (!latch && by > CLICK) { latch = true; svg.classList.toggle('on'); }
      else if (latch && by < CLICK * 0.42) latch = false;
    }
    const ex = AX + bx, ey = AY + LEN + by;
    const slack = Math.max(0, -by);                        // cord bows when the bead bounces up
    const cx = AX + bx * 0.5 - Math.max(-14, Math.min(14, vx * 0.04)) + slack * 0.55;
    const cy = AY + (ey - AY) * 0.55;
    cord.setAttribute('d', `M${AX} ${AY}Q${cx} ${cy} ${ex} ${ey}`);
    const tilt = -Math.atan2(ex - cx, ey - cy) * 180 / Math.PI;
    bead.setAttribute('transform', `translate(${ex} ${ey}) rotate(${tilt})`);
    requestAnimationFrame(frame);
  }
  requestAnimationFrame(frame);

  bead.addEventListener('pointerdown', e => {
    const u = svg.getBoundingClientRect().width / 360;
    drag = { x: e.clientX, y: e.clientY, u };
    bead.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId);
  });
  bead.addEventListener('pointermove', e => {
    if (!drag) return;
    const rx = (e.clientX - drag.x) / drag.u, ry = (e.clientY - drag.y) / drag.u;
    bx = 34 * Math.tanh(rx / 70);                                          // sideways give
    by = ry > 0 ? MAX * (1 - Math.exp(-ry / MAX)) : -10 * (1 - Math.exp(ry / 30)); // rubber band
    vx = vy = 0;
  });
  bead.addEventListener('pointerup', () => { drag = null; });             // spring takes over
</script>

title: Staggered Dot-Matrix Ripple
summary: Each click sends a radial front across a dense grid of squares, and every cell answers after a distance-proportional delay with a damped sine in scale and rotation while cooling from yellow through magenta and violet to slate.
choreography: 0-1.15s: the front expands from the origin at diagonal / 1.15s, so each cell starts distance / speed seconds late and the stagger reads as a clean ring.
First 140ms after arrival: the cell flashes yellow within 45ms, twists up to about 30 degrees and swells to about 1.55x.

140ms-2.3s: it dips to about 0.75x at 0.47s, rebounds to about 1.1x, and cools from yellow to magenta by 0.19s, violet by 0.39s and slate by 0.95s; ambient pulses fire every 2.4s from five alternating origins.
agentPrompt:
Render a grid of rounded squares on a 2D canvas (pitch about width/22 clamped to 13-24px, square = 78% of pitch) and keep an array of ripples {x, y, t0}, capped at 8.
Each frame, for every cell and ripple compute tau = (now - t0) - distance / speed with speed = canvas diagonal / 1.15s; skip tau <= 0, otherwise add scale 0.8 * exp(-2.4 tau) * sin(9.5 tau) and rotation 0.62 * exp(-2.4 tau) * sin(9.5 tau + 0.9), and take heat = max(min(1, 1.25 * exp(-3.4 tau)) * min(1, tau / 0.045)).
Map heat through a precomputed lookup of the stops #262633, #7c4dff, #ff3d9a, #ffe14d; fill all resting cells in one path, then draw excited cells on top with setTransform(cos * s, sin * s, -sin * s, cos * s, x, y) and scale clamped to 0.22-1.9.
Spawn a ripple on pointerdown and every 2.4s from alternating origins while the user has been idle for 3s; cap devicePixelRatio at 2 and rebuild the grid in a ResizeObserver.

<!-- Staggered dot-matrix ripple: distance-delayed damped harmonic per cell, Canvas 2D -->
<canvas id="grid" style="width:100%;height:100%;background:#0c0c10;display:block"></canvas>

<script>
  const cv = document.getElementById('grid'), ctx = cv.getContext('2d');
  const OMEGA = 9.5, DECAY = 2.4, COOL = 3.4;          // oscillation, envelope, colour falloff
  const AMP = 0.8, TWIST = 0.62, LIFE = 2.3, CROSS = 1.15;
  const STOPS = [[38, 38, 51], [124, 77, 255], [255, 61, 154], [255, 225, 77]]; // slate, violet, magenta, yellow
  let W, H, dpr, cols, rows, pitch, size, oy, speed, ripples = [];

  function resize() {
    W = cv.clientWidth; H = cv.clientHeight; dpr = Math.min(2, devicePixelRatio || 1);
    cv.width = W * dpr; cv.height = H * dpr;
    cols = Math.round(W / Math.max(13, Math.min(24, W / 22)));
    pitch = W / cols; rows = Math.floor(H / pitch); oy = (H - rows * pitch) / 2;
    size = pitch * 0.78; speed = Math.hypot(W, H) / CROSS;
  }

  function colour(heat) {                               // heat 0..1 -> slate..yellow
    const f = heat * (STOPS.length - 1), i = Math.min(STOPS.length - 2, Math.floor(f)), u = f - i;
    const a = STOPS[i], b = STOPS[i + 1];
    return `rgb(${a.map((v, k) => Math.round(v + (b[k] - v) * u))})`;
  }

  function frame(now) {
    const t = now / 1000;
    ripples = ripples.filter(r => t - r.t0 < CROSS + LIFE);
    ctx.setTransform(dpr, 0, 0, dpr, 0, 0);
    ctx.clearRect(0, 0, W, H);
    for (let r = 0; r < rows; r++) for (let c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
      const x = (c + 0.5) * pitch, y = oy + (r + 0.5) * pitch;
      let sc = 0, rot = 0, heat = 0;
      for (const rp of ripples) {
        const tau = (t - rp.t0) - Math.hypot(x - rp.x, y - rp.y) / speed;   // stagger = distance / speed
        if (tau <= 0 || tau > LIFE) continue;
        const env = Math.exp(-DECAY * tau);
        sc  += AMP * env * Math.sin(OMEGA * tau);                         // 1.55x swell, 0.75x dip, settle
        rot += TWIST * env * Math.sin(OMEGA * tau + 0.9);
        heat = Math.max(heat, Math.min(1, 1.25 * Math.exp(-COOL * tau)) * Math.min(1, tau / 0.045));
      }
      const s = Math.max(0.22, Math.min(1.9, 1 + sc));
      ctx.setTransform(Math.cos(rot) * s * dpr, Math.sin(rot) * s * dpr,
                      -Math.sin(rot) * s * dpr, Math.cos(rot) * s * dpr, x * dpr, y * dpr);
      ctx.fillStyle = colour(heat);
      ctx.beginPath();
      ctx.roundRect(-size / 2, -size / 2, size, size, size * 0.2);
      ctx.fill();
    }
    requestAnimationFrame(frame);
  }

  const pulse = (x, y) => ripples.push({ x, y, t0: performance.now() / 1000 });
  cv.addEventListener('pointerdown', e => {
    const b = cv.getBoundingClientRect();
    pulse(e.clientX - b.left, e.clientY - b.top);
  });
  const ORIGINS = [[.1, .18], [.9, .84], [.5, .5], [.92, .14], [.08, .86]];
  let k = 0;
  setInterval(() => { const o = ORIGINS[k++ % ORIGINS.length]; pulse(o[0] * W, o[1] * H); }, 2400);

  addEventListener('resize', resize);
  resize();
  requestAnimationFrame(frame);
</script>

title: Generative Curl Flow Field
summary: About 220 ink particles trace the curl of a slowly morphing simplex-noise stream function on parchment, leaving fading sage, sienna, charcoal and ochre ribbons that the pointer bends into a vortex and a click reseeds.
choreography: 0ms: 150 simulation steps are pre-run so woven ribbons already fill the parchment on first paint, then each particle fades in over 500ms and out over its last 700ms.
Continuous: every 60ms a 7% paper-coloured wash fades the trails while the stream function cross-fades between two noise fields at 0.07 rad/s, so swirls morph in place instead of sliding.

Pointer and click: strokes within 0.3 x the short side wrap into a vortex with gaussian falloff and no overshoot; a click swaps the seed, washes the canvas at 20% per frame for 300ms and restarts particles staggered over 450ms.
agentPrompt:
Draw ~220 particles on a DPR-aware Canvas 2D over #f3efe6. Each frame, sample a seeded 2D simplex stream function with finite differences and move the particle along its curl (dψ/dy, -dψ/dx) at 38-72 px/s, stroking a round-capped 0.55-1.7px segment in #7d9471, #b4532a, #2b2a27 or #c8973a.
Fade trails by filling the canvas with rgba(243,239,230,0.07) every 60ms instead of clearing it; fade each particle in over 0.5s and out over its last 0.7s, then respawn it at a random point after 2.6-6.8s or when it leaves the stage.
Add a pointer vortex: within a gaussian radius of 0.3 x the short side add 1.7x tangential and 0.22x inward velocity, easing the vortex centre toward the cursor; when the pointer is away let the centre drift on a slow Lissajous path at 40% strength.
On pointerdown reshuffle the noise permutation with a new seed, wash the canvas at 20% alpha per frame for 300ms and respawn all particles with a 0-450ms stagger. Pre-run 150 steps after every resize so the first paint is already full.

<!-- Generative curl flow field: Canvas 2D, no libraries -->
<canvas id="flow" style="width:100%;height:100%;display:block;background:#f3efe6"></canvas>
<script>
const cv = document.getElementById('flow'), ctx = cv.getContext('2d');
const INKS = ['#7d9471', '#b4532a', '#2b2a27', '#c8973a'];
let W, H, F, t = 0, seed = Math.random() * 1e3, mouse = null, parts = [];

// cheap smooth 2D value noise (swap in simplex for crisper swirls)
const hash = (x, y) => { const s = Math.sin(x * 127.1 + y * 311.7 + seed) * 43758.5453; return s - Math.floor(s); };
const noise = (x, y) => {
  const i = Math.floor(x), j = Math.floor(y), u = x - i, v = y - j;
  const a = u * u * u * (u * (u * 6 - 15) + 10), b = v * v * v * (v * (v * 6 - 15) + 10);
  return (hash(i, j) * (1 - a) + hash(i + 1, j) * a) * (1 - b) + (hash(i, j + 1) * (1 - a) + hash(i + 1, j + 1) * a) * b;
};
// stream function; its curl (dψ/dy, -dψ/dx) is a divergence-free velocity field
const psi = (x, y) => noise(x * F, y * F + t * 0.05) + 0.3 * noise(x * F * 2.2 + 9, y * F * 2.2);

const spawn = p => Object.assign(p, {
  x: Math.random() * W, y: Math.random() * H, life: 0, max: 2.5 + Math.random() * 4,
  v: 40 + Math.random() * 35, w: 0.6 + Math.random() * 1, c: INKS[Math.random() * 4 | 0]
});
function resize() {
  const d = Math.min(devicePixelRatio || 1, 2);
  W = cv.clientWidth; H = cv.clientHeight; cv.width = W * d; cv.height = H * d;
  ctx.setTransform(d, 0, 0, d, 0, 0); ctx.lineCap = 'round';
  ctx.fillStyle = '#f3efe6'; ctx.fillRect(0, 0, W, H);
  F = 2.4 / Math.min(W, H);
  parts = Array.from({ length: 220 }, () => spawn({}));
}
function frame() {
  t += 1 / 60;
  ctx.globalAlpha = 1; ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(243,239,230,0.05)'; ctx.fillRect(0, 0, W, H); // fading trails
  for (const p of parts) {
    const n = psi(p.x, p.y), gx = psi(p.x + 1.5, p.y) - n, gy = psi(p.x, p.y + 1.5) - n;
    let m = Math.hypot(gx, gy) || 1, vx = gy / m, vy = -gx / m;
    if (mouse) {                                   // pointer vortex
      const ax = p.x - mouse.x, ay = p.y - mouse.y, r = Math.hypot(ax, ay) + 0.001;
      const fall = Math.exp(-(r * r) / (0.09 * Math.min(W, H) ** 2));
      vx += (-ay / r) * 1.7 * fall; vy += (ax / r) * 1.7 * fall;
    }
    const x = p.x, y = p.y;
    p.x += vx * p.v / 60; p.y += vy * p.v / 60; p.life += 1 / 60;
    ctx.globalAlpha = 0.75 * Math.min(1, p.life / 0.5, (p.max - p.life) / 0.7);
    ctx.strokeStyle = p.c; ctx.lineWidth = p.w;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(x, y); ctx.lineTo(p.x, p.y); ctx.stroke();
    if (p.life > p.max || p.x < 0 || p.y < 0 || p.x > W || p.y > H) spawn(p);
  }
  requestAnimationFrame(frame);
}
cv.addEventListener('pointermove', e => { const r = cv.getBoundingClientRect(); mouse = { x: e.clientX - r.left, y: e.clientY - r.top }; });
cv.addEventListener('pointerleave', () => { mouse = null; });
cv.addEventListener('pointerdown', () => { seed = Math.random() * 1e3; resize(); });   // reseed
addEventListener('resize', resize); resize(); frame();
</script>

title: Luminous Beam Text Sweep
summary: A soft-edged light aperture slides across heavy display type, revealing a white-hot copy of the letters plus blurred and horizontally streaked bloom layers screen-blended over a dim smoked-chrome copy, following the cursor or a slow sine loop.
choreography: Idle: the aperture glides between 10% and 90% of the stage width on a 7.4s sine, slowing at each end, while the curtain rays sway 1.2% of the width behind the type.

Reveal: a 25%-wide core window shows white type with a tight glow, and a 50%-wide window shows a 0.15em blur plus a 0.42em horizontal streak, both screen-blended, so light falls off smoothly on either side of the hot core.
Hover: the beam chases the cursor with exponential smoothing and no overshoot, settling in about 350ms; on leave it eases back onto the sine path.
agentPrompt:
Stack three registered copies of the headline on #09090b: a dim one filled with a dark chrome gradient via background-clip: text, a white one with a tight text-shadow, and a bloom group holding a filter: blur(0.15em) copy plus a horizontally streaked copy (SVG feGaussianBlur stdDeviation "0.42em 0").
Put the white copy and the bloom group each inside an overflow-hidden aperture (25% and 50% of the stage width) with mix-blend-mode: screen and a static mask-image: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent, #000, #000, transparent). Size the aperture content to the full stage.
Each frame translate both apertures to x - width/2 and their content by the opposite amount, rounded to device pixels, so only transforms change and the lit glyphs stay aligned with the dim ones.
Drive x with W(0.5 + 0.4 sin(0.85 t)) when idle and with the pointer x on hover, smoothing by 1 - exp(-9 dt). Add faint vertical repeating-linear-gradient rays behind the type and a brighter copy of them inside the bloom aperture.

title: Counter-Scroll Bento Marquee
summary: Three columns of micro-UI cards scroll endlessly in alternating directions; hovering a card eases its column to a stop, lifts the card on a scale spring with a #111 border and dims the other cards in that column.
choreography: Loop: columns 1 and 3 scroll up at 17 and 14 px/s and column 2 scrolls down at 21 px/s, each wrapping on one measured set height across three card copies so the seam never shows.

Hover in: the hovered column's velocity eases to zero in about 400ms while the card springs to scale 1.045 with one overshoot of roughly 14% of the step, gains a #111 border and deeper shadow in 160ms, and its siblings dim to 50% over 280ms.
Hover out: the card springs back to 1, siblings restore, and the column eases back up to speed; with no pointer for 2.6s a card near the middle of each column is spotlighted for 1.5s in turn.
agentPrompt:
Lay out three overflow-hidden columns on #f5f4f0, each holding a flex-column track with its card set repeated three times; measure one period as the offsetTop difference between the same card in two consecutive copies.
Per frame add v x dt x direction to each column's offset (columns 1 and 3 up, column 2 down, 14-21 px/s), wrap it modulo the period and apply translate3d(0, -offset, 0). Ease v toward 0 or the cruise speed with v += (target - v)(1 - exp(-7 dt)) so holds never snap.
On pointerover of a card set its column to held, add opacity 0.5 to the other cards in that column (280ms ease), give the card border-color #111 plus box-shadow 0 0 0 1px #111 and animate its scale to 1.045 with a spring (stiffness 420, damping 22, mass 1); reverse everything on pointerleave or when another card is entered.
Mask the column area with a 7% linear-gradient fade at top and bottom, and when the pointer has been away for 2.6s spotlight the card nearest each column's centre for 1.5s in turn.
